newsitem.title: USA: FSA says will insure Pa. school bonds despite bill.
newsitem.headline: FSA says will insure Pa. school bonds despite bill.

text.p: Financial Security Assurance said Friday it will still insure bonds issue by Pennsylvania school districts, despite passage in the state House of Representatives of a bill to end property taxes in one year.
The House passed the bill on Wednesday, but state Senate leaders said it had almost no chance of approval there.

"FSA has examined this bill and has decided to proceed with insurance of transactions that FSA has approved or committed to, and to continue to underwrite Pennsylvania school districts on the basis of all sources available to pay debt service," FSA said in a statement.

In the secondary market Friday, Philadelphia School District 5.50s of 2015 were being offered at a 5.60 percent net. Kenny Evaluation Services priced the bonds at a 5.59 percent yield at the close Thursday.
Penn Manor School District 5.10s of 2010 were offered at 99-1/4, compared to Kenny's Thursday price of 98-27/32.
